title: Mars fabrication, repair autonomy and material-feedstock closure audit for OTA-TEC-0089
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0089 Mars Fabrication Center dossier. Assess: (1) demonstrated and developmental polymer additive manufacturing, metal additive manufacturing and conventional machining for space/remote operations; (2) the qualification, inspection and post-processing burden that distinguishes non-critical tools/fixtures from pressure, structural, ECLSS or other safety-critical parts; (3) powder/feedstock handling, contamination, atmosphere, energy and machine-maintenance requirements for metal AM on Mars; (4) what regolith-based manufacturing can realistically produce and why it cannot be treated as a generic substitute for metallic feedstocks; (5) credible recycling/remanufacturing loops for polymers, metals and electronics; (6) the unresolved chain from Mars resources to sufficiently refined alloy/feedstock material; and (7) wording that should remain [H]/[OFFEN]. Do NOT invent production rates, machine counts, local-industry dates, costs, bonuses, resource yields or NOXIA balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0089 is an uncovered mapped object and its ENTWURF status explicitly depends on closing metal-feedstock provenance, process maturity and the boundary between local raw-material production and fabrication capability.
real_world_anchor: In-space additive manufacturing, metal AM/LPBF qualification, conventional machining and repair, regolith-derived construction materials, recycling and ISRU material-refining chains.
novelty_reason: First source-pinned fabrication-center audit that separates making parts from producing qualified feedstocks and safety-critical hardware.
